title: Console Scoped Launch Mode: Minimal Dashboards, Event Tracing, and Cost Summaries
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Goal: Narrow the Redwood Console surface so we can ship a usable, testable MVP for Q2 that provides actionable cost summaries, a lightweight dashboard overview, and a minimal event-level tracing surface without blocking QA or the pilot customer rollout.

Context: The original PRD included a broad set of dashboards (per-route drilldowns, multi-tenant cost explorer, long-horizon time-series, full trace waterfall UI, and per-token cost breakdowns). Given engineering bandwidth, storage/ingestion costs, and the need to stabilize the runtime, leadership has asked the Console PMs to define a reduced-surface MVP that: (1) preserves core observability for early customers, (2) keeps infra/telemetry costs bounded, and (3) avoids heavy dependencies on upcoming infra work (streaming trace storage, long-term aggregation pipelines).

This ticket captures the scoped launch decisions, acceptance criteria, and next-step artifacts for implementation. The scoped launch mode is intended to be toggled in the backend (feature flag) to allow gradual rollouts and to enable a tighter set of UX flows for the GA milestone.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard landing card set limited to: (a) overall request volume and error rate, (b) p50/p95/p99 latency distribution, (c) top 5 routes by request count, and (d) top 5 cost contributors (model+route). No per-route multi-card view for MVP.
Cost summary card shows 7-day and 30-day totals, delta vs previous period, and an exportable CSV. Per-token-per-route breakdowns are omitted for MVP (link to detailed billing report instead).

Tracing surface reduced to: in-console sample list with trace IDs, basic timeline (start/end, duration, top spans) and a lightweight 'open full trace' link that loads the heavy waterfall in a separate dedicated trace viewer. No in-console flamegraphs or span-level annotation editing for MVP.

Trace sampling capped at 0.5% cluster-wide for the MVP; pilot customers may request temporary increased sampling via support ticket and Dedicated customers can opt into higher sampling via config. Sampling rate and storage retention settings are visible in the console ops panel.

Performance SLOs: dashboard landing must render initial cards (empty or with data) under 1200ms for customers with under 1k routes; cost summary queries must return within 2s for 30-day window on prod infra used during pilot.
Graceful degradation: if the aggregation pipeline is delayed or incomplete, dashboards show last-known snapshot with 'stale' badge + link to raw event explorer. No 500-level errors surfaced to users.
Rollout gating: Feature flag enabled for internal users, stage rollout to 3 pilot customers, then wider GA after 2-week stability window and no critical regressions reported.
End-to-end tests added: smoke test for dashboard load, trace sampling verification test, and a cost export CSV sanity check included in the Console CI job.
Design sign-off: design lead approves compact card designs and the reduced trace list flow (see design link).
Docs: short 'Scoped Launch Mode' doc and an FAQ for customers explaining missing per-token views and how to request deeper insights must be published before rollout.

decision_log: Decisions: 1) Remove per-token breakdown from MVP; 2) Cap dashboard to 5 cards and prioritize latency/error/cost/top-routes; 3) Reduce in-console trace UI to a list + open-in-viewer link; 4) Default trace sampling 0.5% for MVP; 5) Use feature flag for staged pilot rollout. Rationale: speed to ship, cost control, and avoid blocking on storage/aggregation infra.
